title: Minimum Swaps to Sort by Digit Sum
summary: Find the minimum number of swaps to sort an array by digit sums (and numerical values on ties) using permutation cycle decomposition.
approach: Compute digit sums for each element, sort indices by (digit_sum, value) to find target positions, and decompose the permutation into disjoint cycles. Each cycle of length K requires K - 1 swaps.

title: Subarrays Distinct Element Sum of Squares II
summary: Compute the sum of squares of distinct element counts across all subarrays modulo 10^9 + 7 using a lazy segment tree.
approach: Maintain distinct counts f(i, j) as j increases using a segment tree. Increment values for starting indices in (last[nums[j]], j] by 1 and query the sum of squares at each step.

title: Subarrays Distinct Element Sum of Squares I
summary: Compute the sum of squares of distinct element counts across all subarrays of nums using an incremental hash set per start index.
approach: Iterate through each starting index i and incrementally add elements nums[j] to a hash set for j >= i. Add the square of the set size to the running total.

title: Maximize Sum of Squares of Digits
summary: Find the good integer of length num with digit sum equal to sum that achieves the maximum sum of digit squares, choosing the largest number in case of ties.
approach: Return empty string if sum > 9 * num. By convexity of x^2, greedily place as many 9s as possible from the highest place value, followed by the remainder digit, and then 0s.

title: Maximum Alternating Sum of Squares
summary: Maximize the alternating sum of squares by greedily assigning the smallest squares to subtracted odd positions and the largest squares to added even positions.
approach: Compute squares of all elements, sort them in ascending order. Assign the smallest n // 2 squares with negative signs and the remaining larger squares with positive signs.

title: Apply Operations on Array to Maximize Sum of Squares
summary: Maximize sum of squares of k elements after applying bitwise AND/OR operations by greedily concentrating conserved set bits into the largest possible numbers.
approach: Total set bits at each position are invariant under AND/OR. Count bits at positions 0..29, greedily construct k numbers with all available bits, and sum squares modulo 10^9 + 7.
timeComplexity: O(N + K) where N = nums.length, K = k

title: Sum of Squares of Special Elements
summary: Calculate the sum of squares of special elements in a 1-indexed array where index i divides the length of the array n.
approach: Iterate i from 1 to n. If n % i == 0, square nums[i - 1] and add to the running sum. Runs in O(N) time with O(1) auxiliary space.

title: Minimum Sum of Squared Difference
summary: Minimize the sum of squared difference by greedily reducing largest absolute differences first using a frequency bucket array.
approach: Pool total reductions k = k1 + k2. Since (x)^2 - (x-1)^2 = 2x - 1, largest differences yield the greatest square decrease. Use a frequency bucket count[d] over bounded differences (<= 10^5) to step down from maxDiff in O(N + M) time.

title: Minimum Insertions to Balance a Parentheses String
summary: Find minimum insertions required to balance parentheses where each '(' requires two consecutive '))'.
approach: Greedy linear traversal maintaining count of unmatched '(' and required insertions. Consecutive ')' are grouped together, inserting missing ')' or '(' when necessary.

title: Remove Outermost Parentheses
summary: Remove the outermost parentheses of every primitive substring in a valid parentheses string.
approach: Track nesting depth linearly. Only include '(' when current depth > 0 before incrementing, and include ')' when depth > 0 after decrementing.

title: Remove Invalid Parentheses
summary: Remove the minimum number of invalid parentheses to make the input string valid, returning all unique results.
approach: Precompute misplaced '(' and ')' counts to bound search depth. Use DFS backtracking with adjacent duplicate pruning and validity checking.
timeComplexity: O(2^N) bounded by O(C(N, rem) * N)

title: Minimum Add to Make Parentheses Valid
summary: Determine the minimum number of parentheses additions needed to make a string of parentheses valid.
approach: Greedy linear scan counting unmatched open parentheses and insertions required for unmatched closing parentheses in O(N) time and O(1) space.

title: Score of Parentheses
summary: Calculate the numerical score of a balanced parentheses string according to compounding nesting rules.
approach: Track nesting depth linearly. Each immediate '()' pair contributes 2^depth (1 << depth) to the total score in O(N) time and O(1) space.

title: Valid Parenthesis String
summary: Check whether a string with '(', ')' and wildcard '*' can represent a valid balanced parentheses sequence.
approach: Greedy range tracking maintaining minimum and maximum possible open parentheses count [lo, hi]. If hi < 0 at any point return false; return lo == 0 at the end.

title: Longest Valid Parentheses
summary: Find the length of the longest valid parentheses substring in a given string of parentheses.
approach: Index-based stack tracking with base boundary at -1. Pop on ')' and either update maximum substring length (i - stack[top]) or set new barrier index.

title: Generate Parentheses
summary: Generate all combinations of well-formed parentheses given n pairs.
approach: Backtracking ensuring valid prefix invariants: only add '(' if open < n, and only add ')' if close < open.
timeComplexity: O(4^n / sqrt(n)) bounded by n-th Catalan number

title: Valid Parentheses
summary: Determine if an input string with brackets '()', '{}', and '[]' is valid.
approach: Parity check length, then use a primitive character stack to match closing brackets with opening brackets.

title: Maximum Nesting Depth of Two Valid Parentheses Strings
summary: Split a VPS into two disjoint VPS subsequences A and B to minimize max(depth(A), depth(B)).
approach: Assign parentheses based on the parity of their nesting depth (depth % 2) so that alternating nesting levels are distributed evenly between the two subsequences.

title: Check if There Is a Valid Parentheses String Path
summary: Check if there is a path from (0, 0) to (m - 1, n - 1) in a grid of '(' and ')' that forms a valid balanced parentheses string.
approach: Prune early if path length is odd or boundary brackets are invalid. Use 3D Dynamic Programming dp[i][j][b] tracking reachability of open parentheses balance b at cell (i, j).

title: Maximum Nesting Depth of the Parentheses
summary: Return the maximum nesting depth of parentheses in a valid parentheses string s.
approach: Scan through the string using a depth counter: increment on '(' updating maxDepth, and decrement on ')'.

title: Reverse Substrings Between Each Pair of Parentheses
summary: Reverse the strings in each pair of matching parentheses, starting from the innermost one, returning the bracket-free resulting string.
approach: Maintain a stack of string buffers representing enclosing scopes. When encountering '(', push the current buffer and start anew. When encountering ')', reverse the current buffer, pop the outer buffer, and append to it.

title: Evaluate the Bracket Pairs of a String
summary: Replace bracketed keys in a string with their corresponding values from a knowledge dictionary, or '?' if the key is not present.
approach: Populate a hash map with knowledge key-value pairs, then linearly parse the string replacing each bracketed (key) with map lookup or '?' otherwise appending characters directly.

title: Brace Expansion II
summary: Evaluate an expression consisting of curly braces, commas, and lowercase letters representing sets of words under union and concatenation grammar rules.
approach: Recursive descent parser where parse() computes the Cartesian concatenation product of adjacent sub-expressions until a comma or closing brace, and parseSingle() handles union sets inside curly braces separated by commas.

title: Smallest Index With Digit Sum Equal to Index
summary: Return the smallest index i in nums such that the sum of the digits of nums[i] equals i.
approach: Iterate sequentially from index 0 to n - 1, compute the digit sum of each element by extracting digits modulo 10, and return the first matching index.

title: Minimum Operations to Reduce X to Zero
summary: Find the minimum number of operations to remove elements from either end summing to x by finding the longest central contiguous subarray summing to total - x.
approach: Invert the problem to find the maximum length contiguous subarray summing to total - x using a two-pointer sliding window, leveraging the positivity of array elements for strict monotonicity.

title: Find X Value of Array II
summary: Process persistent point updates and count the number of non-empty prefixes of a query suffix whose product modulo k equals x.
approach: Build a segment tree where each node maintains total product modulo k and a frequency array of prefix remainder products, merge children by scaling right prefixes by left product, apply point updates, and query the suffix range [start, n - 1].
timeComplexity: O(N * k + Q * k * log N)

title: Find X Value of Array I
summary: Count the number of contiguous non-empty subarrays whose element product modulo k equals x for each x from 0 to k - 1.
approach: Maintain a DP frequency array tracking remainder counts of subarrays ending at the previous position, transition each remainder by multiplying with (nums[r] % k) modulo k, include the single-element subarray nums[r], and accumulate into the result array.

title: Reverse Degree of a String
summary: Calculate the reverse degree of a string by summing the product of each character's reversed alphabet position and its 1-indexed string position.
approach: Iterate through each character, compute its reversed alphabet position (26 - (ch - 'a')), multiply by (index + 1), and sum the results.

title: Circle and Rectangle Overlapping
summary: Determine if an axis-aligned rectangle and a circle have at least one common overlapping point.
approach: Find the closest point on the rectangle to the circle's center by clamping the coordinates, then verify if the squared Euclidean distance is within radius squared.

title: Maximum Number of Non-Overlapping Substrings
summary: Find the maximum number of non-overlapping substrings such that every character in each substring appears solely within that substring, minimizing total length.
approach: Precompute first and last occurrences of all 26 characters. For each valid starting character, expand candidate windows and select non-overlapping intervals greedily, replacing longer outer intervals with strictly contained shorter ones.

title: Find Two Non-overlapping Sub-arrays Each With Target Sum
summary: Find two non-overlapping subarrays each summing to target such that the sum of their lengths is minimized.
approach: Use prefix sums and a hash map to detect subarrays summing to target, paired with a prefix DP array storing the minimum length of any preceding valid subarray.

title: Number of Sets of K Non-Overlapping Line Segments
summary: Calculate the number of ways to draw k non-overlapping line segments that may share endpoints using a combinatorial bijection to binomial coefficient.
approach: By mapping shared boundary points through coordinate expansion, the problem is equivalent to choosing 2k points out of n + k - 1 points. Computed using Pascal's triangle DP modulo 10^9 + 7.

title: Maximum Number of Non-overlapping Palindrome Substrings
summary: Find the maximum count of non-overlapping palindrome substrings of length at least k using dynamic programming precomputation and greedy interval selection.
approach: Precompute all palindrome substrings using an O(N²) DP table. Then greedily pick the earliest non-overlapping palindromes of minimal valid length (k or k+1).

title: Rectangle Overlap
summary: Determine whether two axis-aligned rectangles have an intersection with positive area.
approach: Check the complementary condition where rec2 is entirely to the right, left, above, or below rec1. Return the negation of this disjunction.

title: Image Overlap
summary: Calculate the maximum possible overlap of 1 bits between two binary images by testing all horizontal and vertical translation shifts.
approach: Iterate through all (2n - 1) * (2n - 1) possible shift vectors (dx, dy). For each shift, count overlapping 1s within valid matrix boundaries and take the maximum.

title: Maximum Score of Non-overlapping Intervals
summary: Find the lexicographically smallest sorted list of up to 4 non-overlapping intervals yielding maximum total weight using interval sorting, binary search, and prefix DP.
approach: Sort intervals by right endpoint. For each interval, binary search for the rightmost non-overlapping preceding interval. Maintain prefix DP tables for choosing up to 4 intervals with tie-breaking for lexicographically smaller index combinations.

title: Unique 3-Digit Even Numbers
summary: Determine the number of distinct three-digit even numbers with no leading zeros that can be formed from an array of digits using permutations and set deduplication.
approach: Iterate through all unique index triplets (i, j, k) with distinct indices. Verify that digits[i] != 0 and digits[k] is even. Add the resulting 3-digit number to a set to remove duplicates, returning the set size.

title: Count Nodes Equal to Average of Subtree
summary: Return the number of nodes in a binary tree where the node's value equals the integer average of the values in its subtree using post-order DFS.
approach: Perform a bottom-up post-order DFS where each recursive call returns the subtree sum and subtree node count. Compute the integer average at each node and increment the count if it matches the node's value.

title: Count Commas in Range II
summary: Calculate the total number of commas used in standard number formatting for integers up to 10^15 using 64-bit threshold scaling.
approach: Iterate through powers of 1,000 using 64-bit integers and add (n - threshold + 1) for each threshold level until the threshold exceeds n.

title: Count Commas in Range
summary: Count the total number of commas used in standard number formatting for all integers from 1 to n by summing threshold tier contributions.
approach: Iteratively add (n - threshold + 1) for each comma threshold starting from 1,000 and scaling by 1,000 each step until the threshold exceeds n.

title: Distinct Subsequences II
summary: Calculate the number of distinct non-empty subsequences of a string modulo 10^9 + 7 using dynamic programming tracked by the last character of each subsequence.
approach: Maintain dp[c] representing distinct subsequences ending with character c. For each character ch, compute total = 1 + sum(dp) modulo 10^9 + 7, then set dp[ch - 'a'] = total. The final answer is sum(dp) modulo 10^9 + 7.

title: Distinct Subsequences
summary: Calculate the number of distinct subsequences of string s that match target string t using a 2D dynamic programming grid.
approach: Define dp[i][j] as the number of distinct subsequences of prefix s[0..i-1] equal to t[0..j-1]. Transition using dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j] + (s[i-1] == t[j-1] ? dp[i-1][j-1] : 0) with base case dp[i][0] = 1.

title: Smallest Stable Index II
summary: Find the smallest index i such that the instability score max(nums[0..i]) - min(nums[i..n-1]) is less than or equal to k for arrays up to 10^5 elements using prefix maximum and suffix minimum arrays.
approach: Precompute prefix maximums and suffix minimums across nums in O(N). Traverse index i from 0 to n-1 and return the first index where prefixMax[i] - suffixMin[i] <= k. Return -1 if no such index exists.

title: Smallest Stable Index I
summary: Find the smallest index i such that the instability score, defined as max(nums[0..i]) - min(nums[i..n-1]), is less than or equal to k using prefix maximum and suffix minimum arrays.
approach: Precompute prefix maximums and suffix minimums across the array in O(N). Iterate through each index i from 0 to n-1 and return the first index where prefixMax[i] - suffixMin[i] <= k. Return -1 if no such index exists.

title: Construct Uniform Parity Array II
summary: Determine if an array nums1 can be converted to an all-even or all-odd array nums2 by optionally subtracting a strictly smaller element of appropriate parity.
approach: Evaluate target parities 0 and 1. If an element does not match target parity, verify that a strictly smaller element of needed parity exists by checking against the global minimum of that parity.

title: Construct Uniform Parity Array I
summary: Determine if an array nums1 can be converted to an all-even or all-odd array nums2 by choosing to keep elements or subtract another element using parity analysis.
approach: Count even and odd elements. All even is possible if oddCount == 0 or oddCount >= 2. All odd is possible if evenCount == 0 or oddCount >= 1. Return allEven || allOdd.

title: Minimum Moves to Clean the Classroom
summary: Find the minimum moves required for a student to collect all litter items in an m x n classroom using energy replenishment areas and obstacles via BFS with bitmask state tracking.
approach: Model the search as a shortest-path problem on a multi-dimensional state graph (r, c, energy, litterMask). Use Breadth-First Search (BFS) starting from S with full energy. When stepping onto R, restore energy to maximum capacity. When stepping onto a litter cell L, flip its corresponding bit in the bitmask. The first state reaching fullMask yields the minimum moves.

title: Smallest Divisible Digit Product I
summary: Find the smallest number greater than or equal to n whose digit product is divisible by t.
approach: Iterate upwards starting from n and compute the digit product of each candidate integer. Return the first number whose digit product is divisible by t. Within at most 10 iterations, a multiple of 10 is reached (digit product 0), guaranteeing O(1) termination.

title: Remove Methods From Project
summary: Remove a buggy method and all methods reachable from it, provided no non-suspicious method invokes any suspicious method.
approach: Traverse the directed invocation graph starting from method k using BFS to discover all suspicious methods. Then check all invocations: if any non-suspicious method calls a suspicious method, abort and return all methods; otherwise, return all non-suspicious methods.

title: Find Missing Elements
summary: Find all missing integers between the minimum and maximum elements of a unique integer array.
approach: Find the minimum and maximum elements in nums, insert all elements into a hash set for O(1) membership testing, and collect all integers from min to max absent from the set into a sorted result list.

title: Stone Game III
summary: Determine the winner (Alice, Bob, or Tie) of a turn-based game where players take 1, 2, or 3 stones from the remaining row to maximize relative score advantage.
approach: Use linear Dynamic Programming dp[i] from right to left tracking the maximum score difference (current player - opponent) achievable from stoneValue[i..n-1] by evaluating choices k in {1, 2, 3}.

title: Stone Game
summary: Determine if Alice wins a stone-picking game where players take piles from either end of an even-length array with an odd total sum of stones.
approach: Use interval Dynamic Programming dp[i][j] tracking the maximum relative stone advantage the current player can achieve over their opponent from piles[i..j]. Alternatively, Alice always wins (return true) because with an even number of piles and odd total sum, Alice can strictly force picking either all even or all odd indices.

title: Predict the Winner
summary: Determine if Player 1 can win or tie in an optimal two-player zero-sum game picking numbers from either end of an array.
approach: Use interval Dynamic Programming dp[i][j] tracking the maximum relative score difference achievable by the current player from subarray nums[i..j].
